faq.q: What is the best month for dolphin watching in Marbella?
faq.a: June, July, and August are the best months. Sea temperatures reach 25–30°C, the Mediterranean is calm, and dolphin activity peaks. Sightings are frequent, especially in the early morning when the water is flat and dolphins are feeding near the surface.

faq.q: Can you see dolphins in Marbella in winter?
faq.a: Yes, dolphins are resident in the Alboran Sea year-round. However, from November to February, winds and rougher seas reduce sighting probabilities. If you visit in winter, choose a calm day and a larger boat like the Mangusta 80 for stability.

faq.q: Which dolphin species are found near Marbella?
faq.a: You'll most commonly encounter common dolphins (Delphinus delphis), striped dolphins (Stenella coeruleoalba), and bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus). Occasionally, pilot whales and even orcas pass through the Strait of Gibraltar area, but they are less predictable.

faq.q: How long is a dolphin watching boat trip?
faq.a: Most of our charters last 2 to 4 hours. A 2-hour trip is enough to reach the dolphin feeding grounds off Cabopino or Cala del Faro. For a more relaxed experience with swimming stops, a 4-hour charter is ideal.

faq.q: What is the best time of day for dolphin watching?
faq.a: Early morning (9:00–11:00) is best. The sea is calm, winds are light, and dolphins are actively hunting after the night. Late afternoon trips can also be good, but summer sea breezes may create choppier conditions.

data.body_html:
Marbella's coastline, with the Sierra Blanca mountains as a backdrop and the glittering waters of the Alboran Sea, is one of Europe's best spots for dolphin watching. The marbella dolphin watching season runs from May to September, but with the right boat and a bit of luck, you can spot these marine mammals almost any month of the year. In this guide, we break down the season month by month, so you know exactly when to book your charter from Puerto Banús.

Why Marbella is a Dolphin Hotspot

The waters off Marbella sit on the edge of the Alboran Sea, a nutrient-rich area where the Atlantic and Mediterranean meet. This creates a feeding ground for dolphins, whales, and sea turtles. The continental shelf drops steeply just a few nautical miles offshore, bringing deep-water species close to the coast. On a typical 2-hour trip from Puerto Banús, you can reach the feeding grounds off Cabopino or Cala del Faro in under 30 minutes.

Spring (March–May): The Season Builds

March still has cool water (17°C), but by May the sea warms to 20–22°C and the dolphin pods become more active. This is a great time for a boat rental in Marbella because the crowds haven't arrived, and the water is calm enough for comfortable cruising. The Azimut 39 (12.5m) is a solid choice for a 2-hour trip, priced at €749, including skipper and drinks.

Summer (June–August): Peak Season

June, July, and August are the golden months. Sea temperatures reach 25–30°C, and the Mediterranean is at its calmest. Dolphin sightings are almost daily, especially in the early morning. Book a 4-hour charter on the Mangusta 80 (€4,719) — it comes with a free jet ski, so you can chase the pods and then enjoy a swim in a secluded cove like Cala Cortés. The 24m length gives you stability and speed to cover more ground.

Autumn (September–October): Still Excellent

September is a hidden gem. The water is still 23–25°C, and the summer crowds have thinned. Dolphins remain active as they feed before the cooler months. October is also good, though you'll want to check the wind forecast. The Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax) is a nimble choice for a 2-hour excursion, and with the season guide in mind, you'll know exactly when to go.

Winter (November–February): The Challenging Months

Winter brings rougher seas and cooler temperatures (15–18°C). Dolphins are still present, but sighting probability drops. If you're determined, choose a larger vessel like the Canados 86 (26m) or the Ferretti 94 (29m) for maximum stability. Skippers will often head toward the deeper waters near the Strait of Gibraltar, where pods gather. Expect a bumpier ride, but the reward is a rare winter encounter.

How to Maximise Your Dolphin Sighting Chances

  • Go early: 9:00–11:00 is prime time.
  • Choose a calm day: wind under 15 knots.
  • Book a 4-hour charter: more time = more chances.
  • Use a fast boat: the Mangusta 80 can cover 30+ NM in a morning.
  • Listen to the skipper: they know the local hotspots.

Which Boat to Choose for Dolphin Watching

For small groups (up to 9), the Astondoa 40 at €749/2h is an affordable option. For families (up to 11), the Azimut 39 at the same price offers a flybridge for panoramic views. If you want the full experience, the Tier B Mangusta 80 (€4,719 for 4h) includes a free jet ski — perfect for getting closer to the dolphins (while respecting their space). All our charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and 21% IVA.

Responsible Dolphin Watching

We follow the Spanish marine mammal protection guidelines: no chasing, no sudden turns, and maintaining a safe distance of at least 60 metres. Our skippers are trained to observe without disturbing. This ensures the dolphins return year after year, keeping Marbella a premier destination for boat charters.
